answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% component spend cut, the incumbent refuses to reopen price this cycle, and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and a 94%-utilized line. Switching primary vendor (c2) saved cost before, but doing it in 14 days while running at 94% is exactly the delivery-risk path the objective says to avoid. Renewing the incumbent (c1) preserves integration and on-time delivery, but won't satisfy the 18% cut. Adding a second source (c3) is the right structural answer to single-point fragility, but qualifying a parallel source inside 14 days while operating near full utilization is unlikely to be dependable and risks dual-spend worse than the incumbent's already-refused price. Deferring (c5) past quarter end preserves budget flexibility but the contract does not auto-renew — deferring creates a supply gap on day 15. That leaves negotiate_terms as the action most likely to cut TCO without raising delivery risk, and c4 is the directly relevant prior evidence: a targeted, benchmarked renewal renegotiation moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms. Before committing, I want to verify c4 in the archive to confirm (a) what the price recovery actually was, (b) whether payment-terms changes were a lever we used last time and can reuse, and (c) the conditions under which the incumbent agreed — because in the current situation the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so c4 only helps if the prior play worked despite a similar initial refusal or via a lever we can credibly re-stage now. If the archived record shows the prior recovery came from genuine benchmarking leverage the incumbent cannot easily dismiss, I will renegotiate with a benchmark-backed ask, paired with payment-term and commitment concessions the incumbent may accept even while holding unit price flat, while preparing a parallel second-source path as a contingent fallback in case negotiation stalls within the 14-day window. If the archived record shows the prior win required conditions we can't reproduce this cycle, I will fall back to a short-term renewal on the incumbent at the best obtainable payment terms and reopen the broader sourcing decision next cycle.
